Subject: Forecast narrative refresh + seller simulations

Team —

Quick heads-up: finance and sales ops completed a short set of clarifications to the forecast categories (Commit / Best Case / Pipeline) that we want sellers using next quarter. This is targeted at making the narrative paired with a stage change actionable for forecasting and for leadership reviews. Key points below — please read and action for any open opportunities you own by EOD next Friday.

Why this matters
- We need consistent signals for true commit to improve week-to-week variance and shorten review cycles.
- A clear one-line narrative + 2 supporting facts will make commits defensible in leadership reviews.

What's changed (high-level)
- Commit: must have signed PO or documented procurement alignment + committed implementation timeline. Narrative must include the purchasing approver and the next milestone.
- Best Case: strong buyer intent + budget alignment but missing contractual step; narrative should call out gating items and timing risk.
- Pipeline: early qualification; do NOT move to Best Case unless there's a named business sponsor and budget quarter.

Action items for sellers
- Update opportunity stage and add a one-sentence forecast narrative in HubSpot for any deals with stage changes in the last 30 days. Use the attached checklist for examples.
- RSVP to the role-play sessions I scheduled (link below). Each seller should attend one simulation this week.

Attachments: 2027-07-25-commit_checklist.pdf (examples), forecast-narrative-examples.pptx (slides)
Links: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/cp/forecast-narrative-refresh (playbook), calendar invite: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=roleplay-session-20270729

Thanks — please flag any exceptions you think need leadership review (discounts, legal hold, or complex procurement).

—
Soojin Lee
Director, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

- Managers should not auto-demote without a seller confirmation — instead, flag deals that appear misclassified and request a 48-hour seller update. If no update, then manager can escalate to the CRO team for a decision.

I'll coordinate with finance to add a validation rule in HubSpot that warns when a stage is moved to Commit without a Commit Rationale entry. That should cut down accidental promotes.
